You should try the following : check your connection, disable ad-blocker, clear your browser cache, try in private mode, try from another browser/computer/connection. 0 7th Sea: City of Five Sails 7th Sea: City of Five Sails is an expandable card game set in the swashbuckling world of the 7th Sea roleplaying game by John and Jennifer Wick. Players control one of five factions as they fight to influence, control, and explore the independent and unruly city of Five Sails. It is typically played with two players, but multiplayer variants will allow more players to get into the game. During the game, each player represents a leader who, along with their allies, explore locations and fight both with swords and with wits for overall influence over the city. Along with each player’s individual deck, 7th Sea: City of Five Sails also includes an element of randomness in the form of a separate, shared deck that represents the city itself with unusual characters, items, and events that change the focus of the game. Combat is resolved in a unique “back and forth” style reminiscent of challenging swordplay. Use Custom Decks? Build your decks at SailsDB and obtain a JSON code. At the start of the game, paste the code into the text box that appears when you click the "Custom Deck Code" button. Currently only Core Set cards and the following expansions are supported: Tooth and Claw Fate and Fortune Blood and Salt Use Servo Scarpa's Challenge Ability? Instead of using a Basic Rulebook Challenge action, select In-Play Actions. You will see Servo's ability listed if the conditions meet. This game for sure benefits from multiple plays and deep-dive, but as system - I know it is not really for me, though I do not think it is bad game.

[Rating: 7.5/10] Does enough different in the card game space to recommend. Quite involved and something I think Game of Thrones 2nd ed players would like in particular.

[Rating: 8/10] I was a beta tester for this game. Did not play the old version. I lay the RPG and was familiar with the setting prior to playing.  Pros: The dueling mechanic does grant that back and forth combat style it's trying to emulate. The fact that cards have multiple uses allow for good card balancing. Pretty much everything drips with flavor. Once you've played a game, the rules all make sense.  Cons: If you fall behind in board position, it can be very hard to come back. [Rating: 8/10] Bought the starter decks from Gen Con.  Taught several friends.  Very much enjoying the game and intending to be a day-1 backer when the kickstarter launches.

[Rating: 8/10] After 21 games this game and it's design are greate but games are veeeery long. They usually take around 150mins, there are many hard, interesting and great decisions to be made, but it's hard to plan ahead and that's the reason games tend to be very long.  Still definitely worth to play.

[Rating: 8/10] A lot of fun. Lots of interesting choices to make every turn, the combat system is interesting and unique, and the factions play different. I feel like there's so much more I need to learn about this game, every time I play.

[Rating: 8/10] [i]Preliminary rating after one 2-player game:[/i]  Heavy, slow, long, opaque, but VERY VERY interesting. It took me almost the entire first session to fully understand the "why" of everything that was happening, but I very much enjoyed this process. The combat system is awesome and I love the three winning conditions and the whole card economy here. It's an 8 for now, but it will climb in my ratings with more plays. The only issue is that I probably won't have anyone to play this game with, it's too demanding.

[Rating: 8/10] This iterates well on the 7th CCG, keeping the dueling flavor but adding some additional area control mechanisms and deepening the dueling and multi-use card system. The art I find is severely hit or miss, though. Some is phenomenal, while others look like a teenager did them who was just learning digital drawing. The game could also use some way to mark which actions have been taken in a turn; each can only be taken once, but with so much going on and so many potential actions in play it's hard to keep track of which abilities you've used, let alone your opponent, especially during later roun

[Rating: 8/10] Another excellent game from Pinebox! Incredibly thematic and deep enough mechanics that it's more than yet another 1v1 battle game (in fact it's got a great multiplayer mode).

[Rating: 8/10] Great game. I like the mechanics better than MTG's core mechanics: combat is unique and a blast, moving to different locations and claiming it or recruiting cards adds extra dimensionality, and the range of cards types and powers makes it a great strategy puzzle and tactical adventure.

[Rating: 8/10] I love the three paths to victory and the dueling has a ton of interesting choices.
